root_cause: The previous A3 service still declared a second KnowledgeStage, KnowledgeDecisionView, and hash-bearing KnowledgeSnapshot. It constructed the pre-A1 form of KnowledgeCapsuleV2, so it neither satisfied the canonical provenance/capability contract nor sealed a replayable canonical artifact. Its promotion gate recorded generic evidence digests without proving the required experience chain.

alternatives_considered.option: Restore default values or compatibility fields on the canonical domain types.
alternatives_considered.reason: That would weaken A1 provenance and capability-scope invariants and would make the old service contract authoritative again.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the service-local View and Snapshot but copy new fields into them.
alternatives_considered.reason: A copied schema remains a competing canonical authority and violates §3 and §7.1.

alternatives_considered.option: Infer a missing platform capability valid_from or applicability scope from retrieval time.
alternatives_considered.reason: Retrieval time is not source evidence. Legacy capability cards without a complete canonical scope are excluded fail-closed.

repair: KnowledgeRetriever now imports and re-exports the one domain KnowledgeStage, KnowledgeDecisionView, and KnowledgeSnapshot rather than declaring service-local copies.

The metadata-only legacy search adapter is converted to canonical KnowledgeCapsuleV2, KnowledgeCandidateRecord, KnowledgeDecisionEntry, and KnowledgeSnapshot values before any Director-visible result is returned.

Every candidate, including excluded and security-quarantined candidates, is recorded in the canonical snapshot; selected candidates have exact selection reasons and their decision-view source digest equals their candidate-record content digest.

The canonical snapshot is sealed in ArtifactEnvelope[KnowledgeSnapshot] with catalog, retrieval-input, legacy-selection, and K2 BlockingCommit dependency digests. Replay recomputes the envelope digest and never searches the catalog.
Raw untrusted text and raw source identifiers are excluded from the Director view and sealed snapshot. Only a synthetic quarantine reference and a non-identifying security-event digest remain.
Conflicting candidates are exposed as Director decision options and are removed from automatic selection.

Promotion now requires and hashes a structured chain: media observation, outcome attribution, pattern candidate, corroborating case, counterexample review, applicability scope, independent evidence verification, and human approval.

checks.name: single_k1_k2_implementation
checks.evidence: A3 tests verify that the service identities for KnowledgeStage, KnowledgeDecisionView, and KnowledgeSnapshot are exactly the domain authorities; K2 additionally requires a digest-bound VerifiedBlockingCommit.

checks.name: replayable_snapshot
checks.evidence: Retrieval returns ArtifactEnvelope[KnowledgeSnapshot], accounts for every catalog candidate, binds decision-view digests to candidate records, and replay rejects a changed envelope digest without catalog access.

checks.name: untrusted_text_isolation
checks.evidence: The A3 injection test proves neither source text nor external raw source ID appears in the runtime decision view or canonical snapshot; only a hash-addressed quarantine trace is retained.

checks.name: director_conflict_ownership
checks.evidence: Conflict exposures retain requires_director_decision=true and their option cards are never automatically selected by the retriever.

checks.name: evidence_gated_promotion
checks.evidence: A promotion fails without verified evidence, human approval, or the required observation-to-applicability chain, and the successful promotion digest binds every chain component.

informational_results.name: compile_and_patch_check
informational_results.command: python -m compileall -q mode_p_vnext/services mode_p_vnext/domain; git diff --check
informational_results.result: All touched modules compile; no patch whitespace errors.

residual_risk: The historical knowledge_flow module remains a read-only metadata search adapter during migration. It is not a Director-facing K1/K2 authority; replacing its remaining legacy catalog storage is a later owner-scoped integration concern. A3 does not run Director, providers, Shadow, media, approval, or production switching.
